newsitem.title: INDIA: Politics drives Bombay shares down in shaky trade.
newsitem.headline: Politics drives Bombay shares down in shaky trade.

text.p: Bombay shares fell in shaky trade on Thursday as hopes of an amicable solution to the ongoing political crisis dimmed, traders said.

Bombay's benchmark stocks index slid 52.58 points, or 1.4 percent, to 3598.30 in afternoon trade on news that the United Front government and its erstwhile ally the Congress Party had adjourned second-day talks to resolve the crisis.

"We have to go back and discuss the proposals with the respective parties. Many proposals are there," Harkishen Singh Surjeet, a United Front negotiator, told reporters after the two sides held 90 minutes of talks.
Speculators sold on news of the adjournment, driving stock prices lower on the Bombay and National bourses.
"It seems like the second round of talks has also failed," said a trader at a foreign institutional investor.

The first round of talks on Wednesday failed to make headway after the Congress, which has threatened to help topple Deve Gowda in Friday's vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament, insisted its chief, Sitaram Kesri, be named prime minister.
"No one is willing to keep an open position ahead of the vote," the trader said.
"The market is speculating on political moves," said Govind Agarwal, institutional sales dealer at Motilal Oswal Securities.
